messages:
Ken (Support): opening an escalation from BetaAnalytics. They report intermittent dimension_mismatch and lots of 429/timeout noise from embeddings endpoint after migrating to our Go SDK 0.6.x. They batch ~50 items (mix of text and precomputed vectors). Ticket# INC-3950.

Ken (Support): customer excerpt:
"We moved to rwinfer-go v0.6.1 and now ~15% of embed calls fail with dimension_mismatch. Also latency spikes and many retries. This started after enabling `BatchSize:50` and using precomputed vectors from a previous model. We only compute embeddings once; we expect stable throughput."

Priya (Go SDK): thanks. Do we have a repro or raw request payload? Ask them to paste the exact JSON they send. Also need to know whether they use json.Marshal on a struct that contains []float32 or []byte. If they used proto or custom marshaller that could change type.

Ken (Support): they attached a minimal repro. Go snippet:
```go
client := rwinfer.New("$KEY")
pre := make([]float32, 1536)
for i := range pre { pre[i] = 0.01 }
items := make([]interface{}, 0, 3)
items = append(items, "query one", "query two", pre)
resp, err := client.Embeddings.Create(context.Background(), rwinfer.EmbedParams{
  Model: "redwood-embed-pro-v3",
  Input: items,
  BatchSize: 50,
  Timeout: 30*time.Second,
})
```
They said the server errored: `dimension_mismatch: expected 2048 got 1536` and also saw `HTTP 429` when scaling up.

Noah (Platform): I pulled the ingestion logs. We received payload like:
```
{"model":"redwood-embed-pro-v3","input":["query one","query two",{"__type":"go_slice","format":"base64","data":"AABAQ..."}],"batch_size":50}
```
So the Go client is serializing the []float32 slice as a binary blob with a __type hint. Our intake used to accept JSON arrays or typed-array objects; the blob path was added for efficiency, but validation later assumed float32 length multiples for pro-v3 (2048). If customer kept vectors from legacy model (1536) we should clearly reject with 400 instead of dimension_mismatch during concatenation. Also our batch fast-path concatenates blobs and numbers and a missing pre-validation caused a runtime panic occasionally which surfaced as 500/429 cascades under load.

Eve (ML Eng): two issues: 1) mixing embeddings from different models -> user error/compatibility; 2) client encoding -> server misinterprets type and ends up with wrong float count when converting base64 back to floats if endianness or float32 vs float64 mismatches. Go default float is float64 in some helper conversion logic. If the client sends float32 raw bytes but server decodes as float64 we get wrong length.

Priya (Go SDK): I see a bug in our marshaller: to reduce allocations we used unsafe to view []float32 as []byte and encoded as base64. We added a __type marker for the server. However older server code expected explicit list-of-numbers for shape inference, and in the mixed-batch case the fallback attempted to decode the same blob as float64. We'll push a fix to the SDK to send arrays as numbers when batch size < X or when mixing text and vectors, or include explicit `embedding_dim` metadata in the same object. Quick fix for customers: change code to convert to []float64 or []interface{} with numbers before calling Create, e.g.:
```go
arr := make([]float64, len(pre))
for i := range pre { arr[i] = float64(pre[i]) }
items = append(items, arr)
```
That avoids the binary path.

Ken (Support): customer also complains their naive retry produced a stampeding herd. They used retries for any non-200 including 429 with no backoff. Now their app does 5 retries immediate which tripled requests to our runners and caused a few transient 503s. They asked for recommended retry/backoff.

Noah (Platform): recommend server-side 429/503 rate-limits and a Retry-After header when overloaded. We're adding that. For client guidance: exponential backoff with full jitter; suggested config: base=250ms, factor=2, max=10s, attempts=6. Also set `max_concurrent_requests` client-side. We're adding `Retry-After` header in the next deploy (PLAT-1134).

Priya (Go SDK): we'll publish v0.6.2 in ~3h with two changes: (1) avoid unsafe byte-path when mixed inputs detected; (2) attach `embedding_dim` for precomputed vectors and validate in client before sending (raise helpful error). Also we'll add a Retry helper in SDK with sensible defaults and docs.

Eve (ML Eng): infra mitigation: add a pre-validate step in ingest that reads `embedding_dim` if present or infers from array length and rejects early (400) with message `embedding_dim mismatch: expected 2048 for model redwood-embed-pro-v3, got 1536 from input 3`. Also change batching fast-path to only use blob-concat optimization when all items are marked with `__type: blob` and claim same embedding_dim. Created PLAT-1135.

Ken (Support): action items for SRE/support message to customer:
- Temporary workaround: send precomputed vectors as explicit JSON arrays of numbers (see Go snippet above) or recompute vectors with redwood-embed-pro-v3.
- Increase per-request timeout to 60s for very large batches.
- Use SDK v0.6.2 when released; until then convert []float32 -> []float64 or []interface{}.
- Implement exponential backoff + jitter for retries.

DeployBot: PLAT-1134 and PLAT-1135 scheduled for canary tonight 2026-03-15T22:30Z.

BillingBot: flagged for potential credit: customer reported 22 failed requests and elevated latency; please route to billing for review.

Priya (Go SDK): I'll post the patch link and release notes here when published. Also adding sample helper in README: `func ToJSONFloatSlice(f []float32) []float64 { ... }` and example retry middleware.

Ken (Support): I'll reply to BetaAnalytics with repro steps, temporary fix, and ETA for SDK patch. Closing loop here once they confirm. Thanks all :pray:
